name: Shoulder padding
summary: A pad of wadding or foam that is set in the sleeve head of a jacket or a blouse, so that the shoulder line is wider and square.
how: Cut a pad of wadding or foam, 1 to 2 cm thick, to the shape of the shoulder.
Sew the pad into the sleeve head between the lining and the cloth.
Press the shoulder so that the line is square and level.

origin.where: Paris, France, and Hollywood, United States
origin.note: Elsa Schiaparelli and Hollywood costume designers build wide padded shoulders into women's jackets in the 1930s.

adoptions.via: Armani and the houses of Milan and New York cut the padded shoulder into the working woman's suit.
